title: Feature branch release queue and annotated calendar (low-touch rapid rollout)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a working sketch for a low-touch, feature-branch-first rollout cadence that blends a small weekly calendar window with an explicit branch queue. Target: teams that ship frequent, safe changes with minimal cross-team coordination.

Goals (why this exists):
- Reduce context-switching by batching small feature branch merges into a predictable weekly lane.
- Preserve safety via automated smoke + telemetry gates, lightweight canaries, and a simple rollback ladder.
- Produce consistent release notes drafts per-queue-run (so product + CS can prep messaging quickly).

High-level flow (annotated):
1) Queue intake (Mon): feature branch owners tag PRs with "release-queue/next" and add estimated risk score (low/med/high) in the PR description.
   - Notes: risk scoring is opinionated shorthand (low = infra-safe, no DB change; med = minor schema read-only; high = schema write, latent infra risk).
2) Preflight automation (Tue-Wed): CI runs extended smoke for queued PRs including:
   - integration smoke (auth flows),
   - perf quickcheck (95p latency on representative fixture),
   - golden-corpus regression on N=50 prompts (only for LLM infra PRs).
3) Consolidation + schedule (Thu): Release engineer compiles the queue, orders by risk and team windows, and publishes calendar blocks for the weekend micro-window.
4) Weekend micro-window (Sat 03:00–06:00 UTC): low-traffic slot. Each merge follows the stepwise rollout ladder below.
5) Post-merge observation (Sat–Sun): 6–24h accelerated telemetry sampling with alerts to the release slack channel.

Stepwise rollout ladder (per PR):
- Merge to canary branch (merge queue processes). Canary exposes 1% traffic for 30m. Telemetry checks: error-rate, p50/p95 latency delta, token-cost variance.
- If pass -> 10% for 1h.
- If pass -> 50% for 2h.
- If pass -> full rollout.
Rollback triggers (examples):
- sustained error-rate > 3x baseline for 5m, or
- p95 latency increase > 200ms and CPU spike > 60% across serving fleet, or
- quality regressions flagged by golden-corpus (precision drop > 5%).

Lightweight smoke checklist (automated first, operator second):
- Abort if any CI smoke fails.
- Verify ingestion and authorization endpoints respond within 2s for sample keys.
- Run sample generation (5 prompts) and assert no toxic outputs and no model mismatch errors.
- Confirm no unexplained SLO degradation in last 30m.

Release notes draft template (auto-populate from PRs):
- Queue run date: {YYYY-MM-DD}
- Included PRs: list PR numbers, short one-line summary, owner, risk tag
- Notable changes: bullet points (user-visible + infra-visible)
- Rollback/mitigation plan: quick pointers (how to revert, temp flags)
- Contacts: release-owner, on-call, SRE liaison

Annotated calendar (example week):
- Mon: PR tagging window opens (owners annotate risk and jira link)
- Tue–Wed: CI extended smoke (auto-blocks fail here)
- Thu: Schedule published (ops channel + calendar invite for owners)
- Fri: Freeze for add/remove; only exceptions via release-engineer signoff
- Sat 03:00 UTC: Micro-window starts (merge queue sequentially applies low-risk PRs)
- Sat–Sun: Observation and optional roll-forward for mid-risk PRs
- Mon: Postmortem notes and release notes finalized

Observability primer (what to watch in first 2 hours):
- Latency heatmap by region and model shard
- Error spikes (5xx and client-side 4xx surge patterns)
- Token throughput and average token size (unexpected jump may indicate input-gen bug)
- KV cache hit ratios for interactive workloads (sudden drop => cache-keying bug)
- Cost delta per 10k tokens (helps detect runaway model selection)

Operator runbook snippets (to keep in pocket):
- Fast rollback: revert merge and trigger rollback pipeline; warm fallback model to earlier pinned version; open incident doc.
- Throttle: reduce canary percentage to 0% (safety lane) while we triage.
- Hotfix patch: cherry-pick minimal PR to address crash; prefer config toggle if possible.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- [ ] Define canonical risk scoring rubric and enforce via CI label validation.
- [ ] Integrate golden-corpus checks into branch CI to fail early for model regressions.
- [ ] Determine acceptable cost-delta threshold per customer tier (prod vs staging).
- [ ] Add automated release-note exporter to Confluence template.

Quick links and references:
- JIRA: JIRA-RLS-3124 (queue framing)
- GitHub: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/8765 (example PR)
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-rls-queue-v2 (formal runbook stub)

Notes: This is intentionally lightweight and assumes most checks are automated. The goal is to let product teams iterate fast while keeping SRE/SRE-plat in the loop for medium/high risk changes. Feedback welcome — will iterate this after two real queue runs.

Unresolved: how to handle cross-cutting schema migrations that touch >1 service — likely require separate blue/green lane and not eligible for the low-touch queue.

Signed-off-by: Evan Park (release engineer)
